name: Amanur Rahman Backup & Restore
author: Md Amanur Rahman

sections.description:
Amanur Rahman Backup & Restore bundles your WordPress database and wp-content files (plugins, themes, uploads) into a single downloadable archive, and can restore that archive back onto the same or a different WordPress install.

Large sites are handled by processing the backup or restore in small steps behind the scenes, so it isn’t limited by your server’s script execution timeout. Progress is tracked server-side, so you can safely refresh the page or come back later and the job continues right where it left off.

Features

  • Full database + wp-content backup to a single .zip
  • One-click restore from an uploaded backup or a previously created one
  • Step-based processing built for larger sites, with no built-in size limit
  • Progress is tracked server-side and resumable if you navigate away
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/amanur-rahman-backup-restore, or install it through the WordPress Plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Backup & Restore in your admin menu to create your first backup.
sections.faq:
Is there a backup size limit?

No limit is imposed by the plugin itself — the practical ceiling is your own server’s disk space and PHP upload settings.

Where are my backups stored?

Inside wp-content/uploads/amanur-rahman-backup-restore/backups/, in a folder protected from direct web access.

Does restoring overwrite my current site?

Yes — restoring replaces your current database and wp-content files with the contents of the backup. Always keep a fresh backup of your current site before restoring an older one.

What security measures does this plugin take?

  • Every backup/restore action requires the manage_options capability and a valid WordPress nonce.
  • The backup storage folder — and every working subfolder, including the scratch folder an uploaded archive is unpacked into — is blocked from direct web/browser access and PHP execution (.htaccess + index.php + web.config).
  • Uploaded and stored archive names are resolved with realpath() and confined to the plugin’s own storage folder before any read, download, or delete — user-supplied paths can’t escape it.
  • Archive entries are validated before extraction to prevent path-traversal (“zip slip”) from a crafted archive.
  • Uploaded files are checked by both extension and file signature, not extension alone.

If you discover a security issue, please report it privately to the author rather than in the public support forum.
sections.changelog:
2.1.0

  • Added: the site address is rewritten automatically when a backup is restored onto a different address (for example a copy of https://example.com restored on https://stg.example.com). Before this, the restored site redirected back to the backup’s address. The old address is replaced with this site’s address in every table — including serialized data (string lengths are kept correct), JSON-escaped and URL-encoded forms, and protocol-relative links. Post GUIDs are never changed, a different domain that merely starts with the old one is left alone, and values that cannot be rewritten safely are left untouched and reported. The rewrite happens on the restored copy before it is switched in, so the live site is never touched until the end. Use the ocwpbr_rewrite_urls filter to turn it off.
  • Note: file-system paths stored in the database (for example /www/wwwroot/example.com/…) are not rewritten.

2.0.0

A major reliability release: backups and restores now work on large sites and restore a site exactly as it was.

Backup
* New append-only archive writer. Every step costs the same no matter how big the archive already is, so large backups no longer stall at the same percentage. Big files are streamed across several steps and ZIP64 is used automatically above 4 GB.
* Large database tables are exported with keyset pagination, so a huge table no longer outlasts the server’s time limit. A step that was cut off can no longer leave duplicate rows in the dump.
* Earlier backups are reliably left out of new backups (exact folder matching, Windows-safe paths, any finished *.backup.zip is skipped) so backup size no longer grows every time.
* Fixed: every “%” in the database was written to the dump as a random “{hash}”, which broke serialized theme/plugin settings and permalinks on restore.
* A full disk or small temp folder is reported clearly instead of silently producing a damaged archive.

Restore
* Fixed: each restore step silently dropped the multi-row INSERT it stopped in the middle of (up to 500 rows). Steps now only stop between statements. Backups made by older versions are repaired automatically while restoring.
* The restored database is first loaded into side tables and switched in all at once, as the very last step, after the files are in place. The live site is never left half-restored.
* Every database query and file copy is checked. Real MySQL errors are shown with the table name, unsupported collations (MySQL 8 to MariaDB) and different table prefixes are converted.
* Safe mode: while a restore runs, this plugin’s own AJAX requests load only this plugin (a temporary mu-plugin, removed afterwards), so half-copied plugins or themes cannot crash the restore with HTTP 500.
* wp-content drop-ins (object-cache.php, advanced-cache.php, db.php …) are copied last. Object cache and opcode cache are flushed after the switch.
* Cancelling a restore removes its side tables and scratch files.

Notices and errors
* “Please review these notices” panel: after a restore the site is checked and any PHP error it produces (message, file, line), missing active-plugin files, a broken theme, or a redirect to another address is listed on screen. A PHP fatal error that stops a step is shown with its file and line.
* “Try Now” always appears after an interruption and continues from the saved position. Requests time out instead of hanging, steps are locked per job, and “Try Now” also fires when the connection returns. Interrupted jobs can be resumed after a page reload.
* Progress bar: the percentage is readable at every value, and the bar turns green on success and red on error.

Other
* Deleting the plugin now removes its jobs folder completely, including the temporary safe-mode file.
* Note: a backup or restore that was started with an older version cannot be continued. Press Cancel and start a new one. Existing backup files keep working.

1.4.3

  • If the internet connection drops during a backup, restore or upload, a “Try Now” button appears and continues from where it stopped instead of starting over.
  • The progress bar now shows the completed percentage.
  • Retried upload chunks are no longer appended twice.

1.4.2

  • Removed an unnecessary conditional require of a wp-admin core file.
  • Working files for an in-progress backup/restore (the raw database dump and the raw extracted files) now live outside the web-accessible document root instead of under wp-content/uploads, in addition to the existing folder lock-down.

1.4.1

  • Renamed the plugin (display name and slug) to be more distinctive.
  • Removed the free/premium backup-size cap — the plugin is fully functional with no locked or restricted features.
  • Hardened the folder an uploaded archive is extracted into against direct web access/execution.
  • Fixed a SQL LIKE pattern in uninstall.php so it can no longer match unrelated option names.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: full-site backup, restore, and progress tracking.
